cards.q: What is Wireshark and what does it do?
cards.a: Wireshark is the industry-standard packet analyzer used to capture, decode, and filter traffic for troubleshooting; it reads pcap/pcapng, uses capture and display filters, and visualizes conversations, flows, and handshakes.

cards.q: What are the main capabilities of Wireshark?
cards.a: It captures from a live interface, decodes into a protocol tree, filters via BPF and display filters, follows TCP streams, exports pcap/pcapng, and analyzes using experts/statistics.

cards.q: What is the difference between a capture filter and a display filter?
cards.a: A capture (BPF) filter applies before capture with pcap syntax (e.g. tcp port 443) and limits what is stored, while a display filter applies after capture using rich decoded fields (e.g. tcp.stream eq 0, http.request) to refine the view.

cards.q: What are common Wireshark display filters and their meaning?
cards.a: ip.addr == X shows host traffic, tcp.port == 443 a specific port, http.request requests, tcp.stream eq 0 one TCP session, icmp ping traffic, and dns.qry.name DNS queries.

cards.q: What does the protocol decode tree in Wireshark show?
cards.a: The decode tree shows each header and its flags at L2 (ARP/MAC), L3 (ICMP/fragmentation), L4 (TCP handshake/retransmissions), and L7 (HTTP/TLS/DNS), plus an expert layer flagging malformed or failed traffic.

cards.q: How do you diagnose common problems in Wireshark?
cards.a: For slowness look for retransmissions, unreachable for ICMP errors, auth failures for 401/403, DNS issues for NXDOMAIN, and latency via the RTT graph; Follow Stream plus statistics accelerate diagnosis.

cards.q: What are the common capture vantage points and why choose them?
cards.a: Source host gives an egress view, server gives an ingress view, SPAN/ERSPAN a mixed view, and a tap a full view; choose the vantage point that matches the question being answered.

cards.q: How do you capture packets on-box on Cisco IOS-XE?
cards.a: Use monitor capture CAP interface Gi0/1 both, set limits and buffer size (e.g. monitor capture CAP buffer size 10240), start with monitor capture CAP start, and verify with show monitor capture CAP.

cards.q: How do you capture packets from the command line with Wireshark?
cards.a: Use tshark with a BPF filter, e.g. tshark -i eth0 -f "tcp port 443".

cards.q: A Wireshark capture shows nothing; what is the likely cause and check?
cards.a: Likely the capture interface/vantage point; check the capture point. Too much data suggests no BPF filter, wrong view needs a display filter, truncated data relates to buffer limit size, and parse failures relate to capture/tool version.

cards.q: What is the difference between BPF and display filters in Wireshark?
cards.a: BPF is the capture filter syntax applied before/at capture, while display filters use a different rich field syntax applied after capture.

cards.q: What tool/method is used to analyze a full conversation in Wireshark?
cards.a: Follow TCP Stream for conversation analysis and the statistics views for conversations/protocol hierarchy.

cards.q: What is the on-box capture command on Cisco IOS-XE?
cards.a: monitor capture (e.g. monitor capture CAP on IOS-XE), checked with show monitor capture.

cards.q: What file formats does Wireshark read, and why does it matter?
cards.a: Wireshark reads/writes pcap and pcapng; portability of these capture formats matters for sharing and analysis.
